witness.note: Narrowed fragment of L1, checked by a standalone verifier with no imports, no floats, no I/O, and no exception-based control flow (the previous failure mode: a try/except could mask a failed check). Rationals are integer pairs with exact cross-multiplication comparisons; the malformed-enclosure check uses a boolean flag, never a caught exception. verify() raises SystemExit(1) on any failed check; normal return = all checks passed. Float-literal inputs are represented at the interface by the tagged string 'FLOAT_LITERAL', exercising the lemma's float-rejection clause exactly.

claim: A standalone verifier (no imports, no floats, no I/O, exact integer/rational arithmetic via cross-multiplication, no exception-based control flow, fail-closed verify() entrypoint that raises SystemExit(1) on any failed check) confirms a finite fragment of L1 on an explicit embedded test suite: exact rational evaluation certifies nonzero residual sign, rational interval enclosures certify sign off zero, and the abort clauses fire on zero residuals, zero-straddling/touching intervals, malformed enclosures, and float-literal inputs. covers=fragment.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
